task_brief: Day 6 of "Human-Centered and AI-Aware Design" (unit 6, grade 7) is a correction and reflection on iteration and documentation. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 40–60 minutes. The unit is working toward: Design and test a tool or workflow that uses no AI or uses AI transparently with human verification. Today's work contributes to that by handling iteration and documentation at the correction and reflection stage, against the unit's wider topics of user research without private data, requirements, prototype testing, and bias and accessibility. This session produces reviewable evidence toward the unit performance task.
primary_task: Correct and reflect on your own earlier work involving iteration and documentation. Build a defect log: one row per error, giving the symptom you or the check observed, the root cause you diagnosed, the specific change that fixed it, and the check that now passes. Include at least one case that failed before the fix and passes after it. Then write what pattern connects your errors — a misread condition, a skipped verification, an assumption about iteration and documentation — and name one habit that would catch that pattern earlier next time. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about iteration and documentation, and it belongs to "Human-Centered and AI-Aware Design", which also covers separate topics such as user research without private data. Close out with this check before you stop: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about iteration and documentation; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. At grade 7 the bar is independent work with reasoning that a reader can follow without you present, plus one stated check you ran on your own result before submitting.

presentation_and_privacy.sandbox_and_credentials_note: Everything in this task runs in a sandbox or on paper. Never use a real password, passphrase, API key, account credential, access token, precise home location, or any real person's identifiable information — invent fictional values instead. Do not sign into, probe, scan, stress, or attempt access to any live, production, school, or third-party system, and do not bypass a filter, licence, access control, or terms of service. Any practice login used in an example must be obviously invented — a silly made-up name paired with a nonsense multi-word phrase — and must never be anything you or anyone in your family actually uses somewhere real. If a task seems to need something real, substitute a made-up stand-in and note the substitution.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any code, asset, or text you did not write must be openly licensed or supplied for this task, and must be cited in a comment or note naming where it came from and what you changed.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: Provide a screen-reader-compatible editor, adjustable font size and contrast, and a complete keyboard-only workflow. An offline paper-and-trace route is available for every task here and is scored identically to an on-screen one.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Never require a real password, private message, precise location, account credential, or identifiable image.
Use approved sites and tools; do not bypass filters, access controls, licensing, or terms of service.
Treat AI output as a draft to verify, not as an authority or a substitute for learner work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting iteration and documentation.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for iteration and documentation follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for iteration and documentation, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for iteration and documentation works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of iteration and documentation, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking iteration and documentation mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply iteration and documentation under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on iteration and documentation rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays inside the same sandbox rules — no real credentials and no live external systems. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
